paths.description: Primary password sign-in archetype and common shared chrome; tested desktop, mobile, dark, reduced-motion, forced-colors, keyboard focus, validation, performance, network, security and memory.
Alternative multi-step credential form, CAPTCHA and instructional-content archetype.
Authentication-provider listing archetype with image links.
Password-recovery journey entry with progress breadcrumb and recovery choices.
Invalid route used to assess HTTP/network failure recovery.

findings.summary: The login surface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in palette and file size to the default desktop capture: white page and white form surfaces remain under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for page, card, text, control and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: Switching authentication methods uses abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across password, e-signature and bank pages found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule; the routes are same-origin MPAs with shared chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared header/navigation/content, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Informational modals are scripted div overlays triggered by javascript:void links.
findings.evidence: The modal probe found .mfp-wrap and .ed-modal DIV elements after activation; the DOM contains zero <dialog> and zero popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> for modal information, a button trigger, showModal(), and native close/cancel behavior.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is tied only to page-level breakpoints.
findings.evidence: The fetched 51 KB stylesheet and runtime probe contain no @container/container-type, even though shared login, navigation and footer components appear across compact and wide layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable login/navigation components containment and use size container queries for their compact variants, retaining media-query fallbacks as needed.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on most links and navigation controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focused visible controls: authentication links, help links and footer links computed to outline-style none with no focus-specific box shadow; only inputs and primary buttons exposed an outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible ring with adequate offset to every interactive element and test a full keyboard focus walk.

findings.summary: The keyboard focus indicator is absent on most links in the reading and navigation order.
findings.evidence: The focus-walk probe shows outline-style none and no focus-specific shadow for authentication links, help links and both footer links, so keyboard users cannot reliably track focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply an unobscured :focus-visible indicator to links and controls, then verify sequential focus order across each authentication route.

findings.summary: Lab LCP narrowly misses the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 2,594 ms (good threshold <=2,500 ms) and FCP 2,294 ms; the independent desktop trace measured LCP 1,756 ms, so the issue is condition-sensitive rather than catastrophic.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce document response delay and prioritize only the actual LCP resource; verify on mobile throttling and with field data.

findings.summary: The main document is slow and three classic scripts execute in a parser-ordered body chain.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded a 1,640 ms document request and three parser-inserted classic body scripts without async/defer; total load was 24 requests and 395,431 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Improve origin response time, load noncritical scripts with defer, and verify the encryption handshake remains correctly sequenced.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 26 KiB estimated savings in common.1.9.5.js, with 51.8% of its 51,930 bytes unused on the password route.
findings.suggestedFix: Split common.js by feature and conditionally load modal/keyboard behaviors only when their triggers are present.

findings.summary: Three images omit intrinsic width and height.
findings.evidence: The images primitive and Lighthouse identify the main wordmark plus both footer logos without width/height attributes, although observed CLS remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate width and height attributes (or aspect-ratio) to reserve image space before CSS sizing.

findings.summary: Distinct authentication and recovery routes all use the generic title “e-Devlet Kapısı”.
findings.evidence: DOM captures for password, electronic-signature, bank and password-recovery routes all report the same title, despite having different tasks; the shared description is also generic.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate route-specific titles and descriptions such as “e-Devlet Şifresi ile Giriş | e-Devlet Kapısı”.

findings.summary: Three content actions are non-crawlable javascript:void anchors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO flagged pass_detail_btn, pass_help_btn and gizlilik_btn because each uses href="javascript:void(0)".
findings.suggestedFix: Use <button type="button"> for dialog triggers; use real href destinations when the content should remain linkable.

findings.summary: Public authentication routes expose no canonical URL and sitemap discovery is unreliable.
findings.evidence: The runtime probe found no rel=canonical or hreflang. robots.txt permits the entry route, while /sitemap.xml returned a branded 503 document rather than XML during recon.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish self-referencing canonical URLs for indexable route variants and serve a valid sitemap or intentionally document why this authentication host is excluded.

findings.summary: The identity-service page has no social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks across the entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate og:title, og:description, og:url and og:image tags; structured data is optional unless an applicable schema accurately represents the service.

findings.summary: The CSP provides little effective XSS containment and session cookies are cross-site enabled.
findings.evidence: Headers report default-src * with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval plus data:/blob:. All three Secure/HttpOnly cookies, including JSESSIONID, are SameSite=None. The secrets scanner match was inspected as a jCryption PEM marker and not treated as an exposed key.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the wildcard CSP with explicit source directives and nonces/hashes, remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline, and use SameSite=Lax or Strict unless a documented federated flow requires None.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy is weakened by unsafe referrer behavior and missing permission controls.
findings.evidence: The response sends Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url, omits Permissions-Policy, and relies on X-Frame-Options without a restrictive CSP frame-ancestors directive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use strict-origin-when-cross-origin or no-referrer, add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and enforce frame-ancestors in the hardened CSP.

findings.summary: The primary consumer authentication surface offers no phishing-resistant passkey option.
findings.evidence: The DOM/runtime probe found no WebAuthn or navigator.credentials use. The site offers password, e-signature, bank, mobile-signature and identity-card methods, but not passkeys; no permission prompts fire on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication as an additional first-class method, with secure account recovery and fallback methods.

findings.summary: The Turkish document declares language correctly but the shared stylesheet is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: html lang="tr" is correct, but stylesheet inspection found 28 physical margin-left/right and padding-left/right declarations and no logical-property strategy; dir is unset.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction explicitly where needed and replace layout-critical left/right spacing and positioning with inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: The sign-in form disables autofill and password-manager assistance.
findings.evidence: The form and both identity/password inputs declare autocomplete="off"; the security copy explicitly tells users to disable browser password saving. The correct tokens would be username and current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove form-level autocomplete=off and use autocomplete="username" and "current-password". Do not discourage trusted password managers.

findings.summary: Oversized legacy PNG logos dominate an otherwise small page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 121 KiB image-delivery savings. The 709×172 security-board logo is displayed around 148×36 and transfers 76 KB; all four images are PNG with no srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve appropriately sized SVG/WebP/AVIF variants, add responsive sources where raster assets remain, and avoid loading below-fold logos at oversized resolutions.

taskList.title: Harden CSP, referrer, permissions and cookie policy
Enable safe sign-in assistance and password managers
Improve mobile LCP and resource scheduling
Give each route unique, crawlable metadata and controls
Respect dark theme and modern responsive components
Replace scripted DIV modals and add route transitions
